The problem here is you have a bunch of people all talking about something they know nothing about. Most of these are 2nd and 3rd hand stories. For example, if you work for a dealership, all of your training is paid for. You actually get paid to go to school. People that are dumb enough to go to trade school and pay all that money for absolutely nothing, should have done a little more research. Or that Ford tech about 8 minutes in with the heater core. I'll take them for 5 hours all day long. I work for Ford, and there's a few people like me who know that once you do the same exact job a bunch of times, you get very fast without sacrificing quality. Everyone does the job one or two times and cries because it took all day. On an F150 it doesn't take me anywhere near 5 hours to replace one. Also, he never took the time to learn how to use Fords billing system. He should be getting more than 4.9, but he has no idea how to bill for it. You don't need 20k+ in tools, especially if you are just starting out. No one forces these kids that are very new to go out and buy a 10k tool box from SnapOn. Thats a choice. You can get something for under 1k that will last you quite a while. 

On this topic, there's more misinformation than good. Everyone has their stories. Most people can't think outside of themselves. They have expeiance doing one thing, or working for one place, and that's the standard set for everyone. They didn't make good money working for Ford, therefore no one can.
